summary:
# NOTES: A MONK OF CRUTA (E. Phillips Oppenheim, 1894; Gutenberg #31535). Single book, no separate volumes.

Publisher frontmatter: J.S. Ogilvie Publishing Co., NY; copyright 1894 F. Tennyson Neely. Ads at end for "The Mystery of the Ravenspurs" (Fred M. White) and "The Peer and the Woman" (Oppenheim).

## CAST
- **Father Adrian**: tall, gaunt, dark-eyed Catholic priest; son of Count of Cruta's daughter Irene and Martin de Vaux (secretly); Jesuit-like; monk/priest of St. Bernard monastery (Cruta). Later "Adrian" to Adrea.
- **Martin de Vaux**: master of Vaux Abbey, dying at monastery of Cruta; shot dead Count Hirsfeld's... (see plot). Owner of Vaux Abbey, 40k/yr.
- **Gomez**: Martin's servant (later Major Harcourt's cottage caretaker); loyal, later helps Adrea.
- **Paul de Vaux**: son of Martin & Lady de Vaux (duke's daughter); tall, fair, grave; ~north-country; author of unfashionable novel; thought he was legitimate heir.
- **Arthur de Vaux**: Paul's younger brother, army officer (Aldershot), infatuated with Adrea; wears violets.
- **Adrea Kiros**: dusky, Eastern-looking dancer; "little brown girl"; ward of Paul; daughter of Count Hirsfeld and Irene's... (actually daughter of Count Hirsfeld, per Madame's account); convent St. Lucile; father murdered by Martin at Cruta.
- **Mrs. de Vaux**: Paul's mother, white-haired, dignified, hunting woman.
- **Lady May Westover**: fair, grey-eyed, Paul's intended; brother Captain Westover (Lord Westover's son); Lord & Lady Westover.
- **Reynolds**: grey-headed butler at Vaux.
- **Richards**: manservant at Vaux.
- **Madame de Merteuill** (= Irene, daughter of the Count of Cruta; real name Irene); step-mother of Adrea in pretence; lives at Major Harcourt's cottage.
- **Celeste**: Adrea's maid.
- **Count Victor Ferdinand Hirsfeld**: calls himself Rudolph/ambassador; Irene's suitor/conspirator; Adrea's father (per Madame's account the murdered man was "Count Hirsfeld"? — text: Adrea's father killed by Martin at Cruta; Madame says Adrea was Count Hirsfeld's daughter).
- **Count of Cruta**: old, tall, white-bearded, feared islander lord, Irene's father; mad, rigged plot; blew up castle.
- **Guiseppe**: old fisherman of Cruta; saves Paul.
- Fishermen: Antonio, Francesco, Ferdinand.
- **Leslie Horton**: with Arthur in London.
- **Cis** (Paul's friend, source of rumours re Arthur). Dick Carruthers (Paul's friend). Lady Swindon (reception host). Denison (club).
- **Father Andrew**: monk at Cruta.
- **Marie**: Irene's dying maid who personated Irene at the false wedding.
- **Gomez/ Harcourt**: Major Harcourt, old half-pay officer, cottage on moor.

## PROLOGUE (Ch. I) — Cruta, monastery
- Martin de Vaux dying in monastery of Cruta, stormy night; servant Gomez, priest Father Adrian. Steamer enters bay; Paul steers boat ashore; Victor (Count Hirsfeld) with Paul arrives.
- Martin says "Victor" — Hirsfeld: "Curse you, Martin de Vaux!" Refuses money offered for his power over "those I love."
- Martin shoots Hirsfeld, dies; a dark child (Adrea) rushes in, sobs over Hirsfeld's body. Both dead.

## Ch. II–III — London
- Lady Swindon's reception; Adrea performs dance. Paul struck. Arthur excited.
- Paul meets Adrea in rain by hansom; she invites him to her rooms (Grey Street, No. 18), revealing "you ran away from convent St. Lucile!" Paul calls her Adrea Kiros. Adrea: "Monsieur Paul."

## Ch. IV — Adrea's Diary #1
- Debut; Paul visited; she invited him to dine & dance; he left abruptly. "you will be mine."

## Ch. V — Vaux Abbey
- Paul returns home; mother; priest (Father Adrian) visited Abbey grounds; Reynolds describes him. Paul haunted by Cruta memories.

## Ch. VI — Hunt; Lady May; Paul proposes thoughts; Father Adrian in avenue; Paul recognises him.

## Ch. VII — Ruins at night; Father Adrian says Martin "died in grievous sin"; "Farewell."

## Ch. VIII — Arthur's debts (Plimsoll acceptance); Arthur's infatuation; Adrea invites Paul for tea.

## Ch. IX — Adrea's rooms; she embraces Paul; he resists; she rages: will ruin Arthur, "I will know my father's secret."

## Ch. X — Mrs de Vaux, Lady May, Paul receives Adrea's letter (18 Grey Street, Thursday; "Monsieur Paul," begs forgiveness; "little brown girl").

## Ch. XI — Diary #2: Adrea finds Irene (woman in black) at Catholic institution opposite (Father Adrian's house); Irene had waited fortnight for Father Adrian; Adrea takes her home; she faints.

## Ch. XII — Father Adrian visits Adrea; Irene reunites with Adrian ("Irene" hug). Adrea: "Father Adrian's rooms."

## Ch. XIII — Paul rides home from hunt; lost way; reaches Major Harcourt's cottage; Gomez answers door.

## Ch. XIV — Paul meets Madame de Merteuill (Irene); she shrinks at his name.

## Ch. XV — Adrea appears; reunion; passion; Paul yields.

## Ch. XVI — Madame furious; Father Adrian arrives, tells Paul to meet him in a week. Adrea: "Beware of him."

## Ch. XVII — Walk on moor; Father Adrian: "Adrea is not for you ... swear"; a week to a meeting.

## Ch. XVIII — Lady May confronts Paul on Adrea; Captain Westover reveals Adrea has £1000/yr settlement from Paul. Adrea calls "cara mia."

## Ch. XIX — Confrontation in cottage: Madame vs Adrea. Arthur arrives.

## Ch. XX — Arthur confronts Paul; calls him hypocrite; Adrea dismisses Arthur; Arthur leaves.

## Ch. XXI — Diary #3: Adrea hates Father Adrian; she follows Madame; Madame is going to Cruta.

## Ch. XXII — Diary #4: Adrea confronts Father Adrian: he threatens; reveals love; rejected; he walks to Vaux Abbey.

## Ch. XXIII — Father Adrian at ruins with Paul; confesses Martin's story (Cruta, Irene, the knife wound from Count Hirsfeld? — Martin wounded in castle, Irene's death alleged).

## Ch. XXIV–XXV — Martin's confession: Irene, Count Hirsfeld, elopement from Cruta, Paris, Irene's disappearance; Martin marries Irene (dying woman, false ceremony).

## Ch. XXVI–XXVII — Martin's Cruta trip, funeral, Hirsfeld's revelation that Irene lives; son Paul's identity and 25-year plan; Irene wrote to Paul.

## Ch. XXVIII — Diary #5: Adrea goes to Vaux Abbey; meets Lady de Vaux; finds Paul stunned in library.

## Ch. XXIX — Diary #6: Paul tells Adrea he is to go to Cruta; Adrea gets Gomez; plots with Gomez.

## Ch. XXX — Diary #7: Adrea walks to monastery of St. Bernard.

## Ch. XXXI — Diary #8: Adrea and Father Adrian (now Adrian) plan flight; Gomez' dagger; Adrea stabs Adrian in chair; body hidden in wood.

## Ch. XXXII — The Lord of Cruta: Count on castle cliff; fishermen; yacht arrives.

## Ch. XXXIII — Paul & Adrea sail to Cruta; Guiseppe warns Paul; fishermen take money.

## Ch. XXXIV — Paul in castle; Madame (Irene) dying; reveals Adrian's birth, false marriage, Marie personating; Irene is Adrea's mother? (Adrea = daughter of Count Hirsfeld and Irene's... note: Madame says Adrea was Count Hirsfeld's daughter.)

## Ch. XXXV — Count of Cruta threatens Paul; castle fire; Guiseppe rescues; Count blows up castle.

## Ch. XXXVI — Adrea's final diary: Paul learns of Adrea's crime; Adrea takes poison; dies in Paul's arms; Paul swoons. End.

## ADS
- "The Mystery of the Ravenspurs" by Fred M. White ($1.25).
- "The Peer and the Woman" by Oppenheim (75 cents).
